## Summary

This turned out to be a very small, deliberately tricky fixture: a single `<h1>` heading plus a two-item image list (`#slides`), with an inline script that duplicates the two authored `<li class="slide">` elements (marking the clones `aria-hidden="true"`) to fake a seamless infinite-loop carousel, à la slick-carousel. The page ships **no CSS at all** — everything renders on plain browser defaults.

Key decisions:
- **Investigated with crow-nester + raw HTML read** rather than guessing: crow-nester's outline showed 4 `li.slide` elements in the live DOM even though the raw HTML (confirmed via direct read) only authors 2 — the classic JS-clone-for-infinite-loop pattern the tool descriptions warn about. I did not treat the 4 rendered slides as 4 real pieces of content to hand-author.
- **Componentized nothing beyond what's there**: the whole page is just a heading + a list; there was no repeated structural fragment worth a red-twine call beyond what was already obvious from the 2-item source, and no ambiguity about whether occurrences shared purpose.
- **No windtailor/Tailwind pass**: since the source has zero stylesheet and no computed values worth extracting (pure UA defaults), building a dynamic Tailwind config would have meant inventing styling that isn't there. I flagged this reasoning explicitly rather than fabricating a design system.
- **Images**: kept the original relative `src` paths (`/product-1.jpg`, `/product-2.jpg`) and exact `alt` text verbatim rather than rehosting or inventing placeholders, per the hotlink-only rule — both original and clone show identical broken-image icons since neither resolves in this file:// context, which is expected and consistent.
- **Fidelity check**: reproduced the exact markup and the exact clone script verbatim (this was the safest and most literal way to guarantee the JS-driven duplication behavior matched). Screenshotted both original and clone at the same 1280×900 viewport, compared them side by side, and ran odiff — result was **0 pixel difference**, an exact match. One round was sufficient given the page's simplicity; no further iteration was needed.

Output written to `/var/folders/gb/m6478s0n5mx9wqlz8t_c03800000gn/T/gumshoe-agent-run-Lu0Fp1/clone.html`. Screenshots (`original.png`, `clone-round1.png`) are saved in that same directory.
